sources.note: A training-free, inference-time unlearning method for RL-trained multimodal reasoning models that detects memorized private attributes from a token-level entropy signature and replaces the committed tokens with image-grounded sanitized embeddings.
sources.title: LEMUR: Latent Entropy-aware Multimodal Unlearning via Visual-anchored Reasoning Redirection

sources.note: ARES trains multimodal reasoning models to spend exploration effort in proportion to problem difficulty, using sliding-window token entropy as the signal for when and how much to explore.
sources.title: ARES: Multimodal Adaptive Reasoning via Difficulty-Aware Token-Level Entropy Shaping

sources.note: DR2Seg splits reasoning segmentation into a description stage and a referring-segmentation stage and rewards the model when a shorter self-contained description still yields the right mask, cutting reasoning length while raising gIoU.
sources.title: DR$^2$Seg: Decomposed Two-Stage Rollouts for Efficient Reasoning Segmentation in Multimodal Large Language Models

result.definition: Qwen2.5-VL is a vision-language model that archived papers train and evaluate on, not a concept, method or dataset; the wiki has no kind for a model, so it is filed under the least wrong of the three available. ARES uses it at 3B and 7B as the base for difficulty-aware entropy-shaped RL, with ARES-7B averaging 55.9 pass@1 over ten multimodal benchmarks against 46.2 for the Vision-G1 baseline, the largest gap on MathVision (51.9 vs 31.3). DR2Seg also builds on it at 3B and 7B for reasoning segmentation, reaching gIoU 68.5 on ReasonSeg validation and 66.1 on test against VisionReasoner's 65.4 and 62.3, while cutting reasoning tokens from 85.3 to 26.9. LEMUR names it among the RL-trained multimodal reasoning models in scope, but reports its unlearning numbers on R1-Onevision-7B rather than on Qwen2.5-VL.
